- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 15–30% for spikes.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast lows by 10–25% to avoid missing downside reversals.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon (days 1–5) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive — apply a 10–20% downward bias to first 5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 5x mean), model often overcorrects; cap forecast at 2x prior peak or 1.5x true outcome if sentiment turns negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term volatility (e.g., alternating 0.67/0.00), model exhibits mean-reversion bias — adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day average, not 30-day.
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤ 0.33) over 3–5 days, model underestimates true volatility — increase forecast standard deviation by 15–20% for next 5 days.
- Model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum shifts — if sentiment turns sharply positive after 3 days, increase forecast slope by 20–30% for next 7 days.
